payload.analysis: Combined with the suspicion of post-encephalitic sequelae, imaging reveals right cerebral hemisphere atrophy and encephalomalacia in the right frontal and temporal lobes on CT and MRI, consistent with prior encephalitis scarring; EEG shows right temporal slow waves without epileptiform discharges, supporting residual organic dysfunction rather than active epilepsy. These findings confirm an acquired structural sequelae and argue against migraine or anxiety as primary. All key imaging information is covered.

payload.analysis: 结合当前最可信的脑炎后遗症假说，MRI显示右侧大脑半球萎缩及额颞叶脑软化，EEG示右侧颞区慢波增多而无痫样放电，支持既往脑炎所致器质性结构及电生理异常；正常神经系统查体和无遗传倾向进一步符合获得性非遗传病因，认知损害亦与脑炎后遗症一致。尽管脑脊液/血清学及正式神经心理评估未获取，但现有影像和电生理已覆盖核心验证信息，可基本排除颅内占位性病变，偏头痛与焦虑障碍因缺乏相应器质性依据而居次。所有关键可获取信息已覆盖，建议临床随访并完善认知康复评估。

payload.report: The patient's episodic symptoms and cognitive impairment are best explained by post-encephalitic sequelae. Childhood encephalitis with subsequent seizures and MMSE 21 indicate prior brain injury. CT/MRI showing right hemisphere atrophy/encephalomalacia and EEG showing right temporal slow waves without epileptiform discharges confirm structural scarring and refute active epilepsy, migraine, anxiety/somatoform disorder, and intracranial space-occupying lesion. Thus the picture reflects residual organic dysfunction from prior encephalitis; no further refinement is needed.
